dimensions.name: Knowledge Delta
dimensions.justification: Provides many expert‑only details (cost‑data lag hours, exact SNS policy statement, auto‑adjusting budget semantics, hard quota of 11 notifications, RI/SP budget type nuances, and a step‑by‑step audit decision tree). These facts are not generally known by a baseline model, but most of the content could be derived from AWS documentation, so it falls short of a perfect 20.

dimensions.name: Mindset + Appropriate Procedures
dimensions.justification: Encodes AWS‑specific procedures: pagination of describe‑budgets, forced us‑east‑1 region, required IAM permissions, organization‑level payer budget handling, and explicit pre‑flight checks. Missing only a concrete step for checking the 11‑notification limit before adding new notifications.

dimensions.name: Anti-Pattern Quality
dimensions.justification: Contains a thorough NEVER list with concrete reasoning (e.g., silent SNS policy failure, decorative budgets, single‑threshold danger, cost‑data lag). Only minor omission: no explicit NEVER rule about unconfirmed email subscriptions, which is mentioned elsewhere but not in the NEVER block.

dimensions.name: Specification Compliance
dimensions.justification: Frontmatter is complete, description, keywords, activation triggers, and invocation schema are present, giving an agent clear when to invoke. Lacks a concrete example of the expected JSON/YAML input structure, which would make activation 100% reliable.

dimensions.name: Progressive Disclosure
dimensions.justification: Top‑level sections (Mindset, Quick reference, Process) give a concise overview, with deeper details (deep reference, remediation) later. However the document is dense; some critical rules (e.g., SNS policy check) are buried in the long “Step 3” description, creating potential cognitive overload.

dimensions.name: Freedom Calibration
dimensions.justification: Calibrates freedom well: read‑only audit steps are permissive, while any state‑changing remediation requires explicit CONFIRM prompts, additive changes, and backup of policies. No over‑constraining of creative audit tasks.

dimensions.name: Pattern Recognition
dimensions.justification: Follows a recognizable pattern (Mindset → Quick reference → Pre‑flight → Process → Output → Edge‑cases → Anti‑patterns → Safety checks → Remediation). Minor inconsistency in ordering of safety checks vs remediation makes it slightly ad‑hoc.

dimensions.name: Practical Usability
dimensions.justification: Provides a clear decision tree, output format, CLI remediation snippets, and worked examples that let an agent execute the audit end‑to‑end. Slight weakness: the exact field names for ActualSpend vs ForecastedSpend in the Budgets API response are not spelled out, which could cause ambiguity in implementation.
